title: 2 Corinthians Chapter 2 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Corinthians chapter 2 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Corinthians Chapter 2 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Corinthians Chapter 2.

questions.question: In 2 Corinthians 2, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: I would not come again to you in heaviness
I wrote unto you with many tears
questions.correctAnswer: I would not come again to you in heaviness
questions.explanation: This statement appears in 2 Corinthians 2:1, which is the first verse in the chapter.

questions.question: According to 2 Corinthians 2:1, what did Paul determine about coming again to the Corinthians?
options: That he would not come again to them in heaviness
That he would bring joy when he came
That he would not come again at all
questions.correctAnswer: That he would not come again to them in heaviness
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 2:1 states Paul determined not to come again to them in heaviness.

questions.question: Who, according to 2 Corinthians 2:2, makes Paul glad if he makes the Corinthians sorry?
options: The same which is made sorry by him
questions.correctAnswer: The same which is made sorry by him
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 2:2 says that if Paul makes them sorry, the one who makes him glad is the same which is made sorry by him.

questions.question: Why did Paul write to the Corinthians according to 2 Corinthians 2:3?
options: So that he would not have sorrow from those he should rejoice in
questions.correctAnswer: So that he would not have sorrow from those he should rejoice in
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 2:3 explains Paul wrote so that he would not have sorrow from those he ought to rejoice in.

questions.question: What does Paul say about his joy in 2 Corinthians 2:3?
options: His joy is the joy of them all
His joy is separate from theirs
His joy depends on his success
questions.correctAnswer: His joy is the joy of them all
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 2:3 states Paul has confidence that his joy is the joy of them all.

questions.question: What did Paul write to the Corinthians out of, as stated in 2 Corinthians 2:4?
options: Much affliction and anguish of heart
questions.correctAnswer: Much affliction and anguish of heart
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 2:4 says Paul wrote out of much affliction and anguish of heart.

questions.question: What accompanied Paul's writing to the Corinthians, according to 2 Corinthians 2:4?
questions.correctAnswer: Many tears
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 2:4 states Paul wrote with many tears.

questions.question: According to 2 Corinthians 2:4, why did Paul write to the Corinthians with tears?
options: Not that they should be grieved, but to know his love more abundantly
questions.correctAnswer: Not that they should be grieved, but to know his love more abundantly
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 2:4 explains Paul wrote not to grieve them but so they might know his abundant love.

questions.question: In 2 Corinthians 2:5, who does Paul say has caused grief?
questions.correctAnswer: Any who have caused grief
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 2:5 refers to any who have caused grief.

questions.question: What does Paul say about the grief caused to him in 2 Corinthians 2:5?
options: He has been grieved, but only in part
He was not grieved at all
questions.correctAnswer: He has been grieved, but only in part
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 2:5 states that Paul was grieved, but only in part.

questions.question: According to 2 Corinthians 2:6, what is sufficient punishment for the man who caused grief?
questions.correctAnswer: The punishment inflicted by many
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 2:6 says the punishment inflicted by many is sufficient for such a man.

questions.question: True or False: Paul wrote to the Corinthians so they would not be grieved but to know his abundant love.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 2:4 states Paul wrote not that they should be grieved, but that they might know his abundant love.

questions.question: True or False: Paul expressed confidence that his joy is the joy of all the Corinthians.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 2:3 says Paul had confidence that his joy is the joy of them all.

questions.question: True or False: The text says Paul wrote to the Corinthians to command them to fast.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Nowhere in 2 Corinthians 2:1-6 does Paul mention commanding fasting.

questions.question: True or False: The chapter states that Paul was fully grieved by those who caused grief.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 2:5 states Paul was grieved, but only in part, not fully grieved.

medium.title: 2 Corinthians Chapter 2 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Corinthians Chapter 2 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to 2 Corinthians 2:7, what should believers do to prevent someone from being overwhelmed by sorrow?
questions.correctAnswer: Forgive and comfort him
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 2:7 states that believers ought to forgive and comfort him so that he is not swallowed up with overmuch sorrow.

questions.question: What does 2 Corinthians 2:8 promise will happen if believers confirm their love toward the person mentioned in 2 Corinthians 2:7?
options: He will be comforted and restored
He will be made sorrowful again
questions.correctAnswer: He will be comforted and restored
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 2:8 urges believers to confirm their love toward him, which relates to comforting and supporting him as stated in 2 Corinthians 2:7.

questions.question: Why did Paul say he wrote to the Corinthians, as mentioned in 2 Corinthians 2:9?
options: To know the proof of their obedience in all things
To boast about his own ministry
questions.correctAnswer: To know the proof of their obedience in all things
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 2:9 clearly states Paul wrote to know the proof of their obedience in all things.

questions.question: How does 2 Corinthians 2:10 connect with the theme of forgiveness in the previous verses?
options: Paul forgives in the person of Christ, reinforcing the call to forgive
Paul discusses punishment instead of forgiveness
questions.correctAnswer: Paul forgives in the person of Christ, reinforcing the call to forgive
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 2:10 explains that Paul forgives anyone forgiven by the Corinthians, and he does so in the person of Christ, continuing the theme of forgiveness from preceding verses.

questions.question: What practical reason does Paul give in 2 Corinthians 2:11 for being vigilant against unforgiveness?
options: To prevent Satan from getting an advantage
questions.correctAnswer: To prevent Satan from getting an advantage
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 2:11 warns that unforgiveness can allow Satan to get an advantage over believers, so vigilance is necessary.

questions.question: What does Paul mean by ‘we are not ignorant of his devices’ in 2 Corinthians 2:11?
options: Believers are aware of Satan’s schemes
Believers are unaware of spiritual matters
Believers rely only on human wisdom
questions.correctAnswer: Believers are aware of Satan’s schemes
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 2:11 states that believers are not ignorant of Satan’s devices, meaning they recognize his tactics.

questions.question: How does Paul describe his experience when arriving at Troas in 2 Corinthians 2:12?
options: A door was opened unto him of the Lord to preach the gospel
He was rejected by the people
He found no opportunity to preach
questions.correctAnswer: A door was opened unto him of the Lord to preach the gospel
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 2:12 describes how Paul found an open door from the Lord to preach in Troas.

questions.question: In 2 Corinthians 2:1, what did Paul determine regarding his visit to the Corinthians?
options: He would not come again to them in heaviness
He would come with harsh words
He would avoid them for a long time
questions.correctAnswer: He would not come again to them in heaviness
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 2:1 says Paul determined not to come again to them in heaviness, indicating his desire for a joyful visit.

questions.question: According to 2 Corinthians 2:4, why did Paul write to the Corinthians with many tears?
options: So they might know the abundance of his love
questions.correctAnswer: So they might know the abundance of his love
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 2:4 says Paul wrote with many tears not to grieve but to express his abundant love for them.

questions.question: What does Paul say about the punishment inflicted on the one who caused grief in 2 Corinthians 2:6?
questions.correctAnswer: It is sufficient
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 2:6 states that the punishment inflicted by many is sufficient for the man who caused grief.

questions.question: How does Paul describe the grief caused by the one who offended, according to 2 Corinthians 2:5?
options: It grieved Paul only in part, so as not to overcharge the others
It grieved Paul deeply and fully
It caused Paul to leave the church
questions.correctAnswer: It grieved Paul only in part, so as not to overcharge the others
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 2:5 explains that the grief caused did not grieve Paul fully but only in part to avoid burdening the whole church.

questions.question: Why does Paul say he forgave anyone forgiven by the Corinthians, according to 2 Corinthians 2:10?
options: For their sakes, in the person of Christ
questions.correctAnswer: For their sakes, in the person of Christ
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 2:10 states Paul forgave for their sakes, in the person of Christ, showing the spiritual unity in forgiveness.

questions.question: True or False: According to 2 Corinthians 2:2, Paul makes the Corinthians sorry so he may be glad.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 2:2 says that if Paul makes them sorry, he is glad because it means they have been corrected.

questions.question: True or False: 2 Corinthians 2:7 instructs believers to punish the person who caused sorrow more severely.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 2:7 instructs believers to forgive and comfort the person, not to punish him more severely.

questions.question: True or False: 2 Corinthians 2:9 indicates Paul wrote to boast about his authority over the Corinthians.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 2:9 states Paul wrote to test their obedience, not to boast about his authority.

hard.title: 2 Corinthians Chapter 2 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Corinthians Chapter 2.

questions.question: What caused Paul to have no rest in his spirit?
options: He was worried about the church
questions.correctAnswer: He could not find Titus
questions.explanation: This is stated in 2 Corinthians 2:13, where Paul expresses his concern regarding Titus.

questions.question: To whom does God cause us to triumph?
questions.correctAnswer: In Christ
questions.explanation: According to 2 Corinthians 2:14, God causes us to triumph in Christ.

questions.question: What does Paul mean by 'savour' in relation to God?
questions.correctAnswer: A sweet aroma
questions.explanation: In 2 Corinthians 2:15, Paul describes believers as a sweet savour of Christ to God.

questions.question: What is the result of being the savour of death unto death?
questions.correctAnswer: It brings condemnation
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 2:16 explains that to some, we are the savour of death unto death.

questions.question: What does Paul mean by 'corrupt the word of God'?
questions.correctAnswer: To preach it for profit
questions.explanation: In 2 Corinthians 2:17, Paul contrasts sincere preaching from those who corrupt God's word.

questions.question: What is the implication of speaking in the sight of God?
questions.correctAnswer: It shows accountability
questions.explanation: Paul highlights in 2 Corinthians 2:17 that speaking in God's sight denotes a level of sincerity and accountability.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'savour' (οσμή) in 2 Corinthians 2:15 mean?
questions.correctAnswer: Fragrance
questions.explanation: The Greek word 'οσμή' (savour) refers to a pleasant fragrance, indicating the positive impact of believers.

questions.question: Which literary technique is used in 2 Corinthians 2:16 when contrasting life and death?
questions.correctAnswer: Antithesis
questions.explanation: The contrast between life and death in 2 Corinthians 2:16 exemplifies antithesis, highlighting opposing ideas.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage relates to the theme of triumphing in God?
questions.correctAnswer: Exodus 15:2
questions.explanation: Exodus 15:2 reflects on God being a source of strength and triumph, connecting with 2 Corinthians 2:14.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the concept of being a sweet savour unto God?
questions.correctAnswer: Ephesians 5:2
questions.explanation: Ephesians 5:2 speaks about Christ's sacrifice as a sweet-smelling savour, paralleling 2 Corinthians 2:15.

questions.question: What precedes Paul's statement about his lack of rest in 2 Corinthians 2:13?
questions.correctAnswer: His visit to Troas
questions.explanation: In 2 Corinthians 2:12, Paul mentions his arrival in Troas before discussing his lack of rest in 2:13.

questions.question: Which verse emphasizes the need for forgiveness within the church?
questions.correctAnswer: 2 Corinthians 2:10
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 2:10 emphasizes the importance of forgiveness, showing the relational dynamics within the church.

questions.question: To whom does Paul refer when he mentions having confidence in the church?
questions.correctAnswer: The Corinthians
questions.explanation: In 2 Corinthians 2:3, Paul expresses his confidence in the Corinthians, indicating his trust in them.

questions.question: Is it true that Paul had joy in his heart despite writing with anguish?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Paul reveals in 2 Corinthians 2:4 that despite his anguish, he wrote to show his love, indicating a complex emotional state.

questions.question: Is it false that Paul sought to cause grief among the Corinthians?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: In 2 Corinthians 2:2, Paul clarifies that causing sorrow was not his intention, highlighting his pastoral care.

theological.title: 2 Corinthians Chapter 2 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Corinthians Chapter 2 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Corinthians 2:4 teach about the nature of Christian love?
options: Christian love is expressed through discipline and correction motivated by deep affection
Christian love requires avoidance of all sorrow and pain
Christian love is conditional upon human perfection
Christian love is primarily a doctrinal assent without emotional involvement
questions.correctAnswer: Christian love is expressed through discipline and correction motivated by deep affection
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 2:4 explains Paul wrote with many tears not to grieve but to demonstrate the abundant love he has toward the believers, indicating love expressed through correction is motivated by deep affection.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Corinthians 2:10 teach about the role of forgiveness in the Christian community?
options: Forgiveness in the community is enacted in union with Christ's person and authority
Forgiveness is optional and purely emotional without spiritual significance
Forgiveness is a human act independent of divine involvement
Forgiveness must always be public and accompanied by punishment
questions.correctAnswer: Forgiveness in the community is enacted in union with Christ's person and authority
questions.explanation: Verse 10 states that Paul forgives 'in the person of Christ' for the sake of the community, teaching that forgiveness in the church is exercised in union with Christ.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Corinthians 2:11 teach about spiritual warfare and Christian vigilance?
options: Believers must be aware of Satan's schemes to avoid being outwitted
Satan has no influence over believers once they are saved
Spiritual warfare is an outdated concept irrelevant to the church
Victory over Satan comes without any need for vigilance or discernment
questions.correctAnswer: Believers must be aware of Satan's schemes to avoid being outwitted
questions.explanation: Verse 11 warns believers not to be ignorant of Satan's devices, teaching the necessity of vigilance in spiritual warfare.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 2 Corinthians 2:14 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: Verse 14 describes God as the one who 'always causeth us to triumph,' showing His sovereign control over victory in Christ.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 2 Corinthians 2:4 specifically demonstrate through Paul's ministry?
questions.correctAnswer: Longsuffering
questions.explanation: Paul's writing 'with many tears' out of affliction and anguish (v.4) illustrates God's longsuffering patience in dealing with His people.

questions.question: How does 2 Corinthians 2:7–8 connect with the broader biblical theme of restoration after discipline?
options: It teaches that restoration follows repentance and forgiveness to prevent overwhelming sorrow
It denies the possibility of restoration after discipline
It promotes permanent exclusion of sinners from the community
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches that restoration follows repentance and forgiveness to prevent overwhelming sorrow
questions.explanation: Verses 7–8 urge forgiveness and comfort of the repentant sinner to prevent being overwhelmed by sorrow, echoing the biblical theme of restoration after discipline (cf. Luke 15:11-32).

questions.question: In what way does 2 Corinthians 2:15–16 anticipate the dual final destinies of humanity found elsewhere in Scripture?
options: By describing believers as a 'savour of life' and unbelievers as a 'savour of death'
By emphasizing universal salvation without judgment
By rejecting any distinction between saved and lost
By stating that all will ultimately perish
questions.correctAnswer: By describing believers as a 'savour of life' and unbelievers as a 'savour of death'
questions.explanation: Verses 15–16 illustrate the dual effect of the gospel, reflecting the biblical doctrine of final judgment and eternal destinies (cf. Matthew 25:46).

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 2 Corinthians 2:10 and 2 Corinthians 2:11 teach about Christian forgiveness and spiritual warfare?
options: Forgiveness exercised in Christ's authority protects the community from Satan's schemes
Forgiveness weakens the church and gives advantage to Satan
Spiritual warfare requires withholding forgiveness for discipline
Forgiveness and spiritual warfare are unrelated issues
questions.correctAnswer: Forgiveness exercised in Christ's authority protects the community from Satan's schemes
questions.explanation: Verse 10 links forgiveness with Christ's person, and verse 11 highlights the need to avoid Satan's advantage, teaching that proper forgiveness guards against demonic exploitation.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 2 Corinthians 2:1 and 2 Corinthians 2:4 teach about the relationship between apostolic ministry and suffering?
options: Apostolic ministry involves self-determined restraint motivated by concern to avoid causing sorrow
Apostolic ministry is free from any suffering or sorrow
Apostolic ministry should always be joyful and never involve tears
questions.correctAnswer: Apostolic ministry involves self-determined restraint motivated by concern to avoid causing sorrow
questions.explanation: Verse 1 shows Paul's determination not to come in heaviness, and verse 4 reveals his tears arising from affliction, teaching that ministry involves self-restraint and suffering motivated by love.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 2 Corinthians 2:5 and 2 Corinthians 2:6 teach about church discipline?
options: Church discipline is sufficient when inflicted by many and should not be excessive
Discipline should be harsh and punitive beyond measure
Discipline is unnecessary in the church
Discipline must always be administered by a single leader
questions.correctAnswer: Church discipline is sufficient when inflicted by many and should not be excessive
questions.explanation: Verse 5 shows grief caused is partial, not to overcharge all, and verse 6 states the punishment inflicted by many is sufficient, teaching measured and communal church discipline.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that 2 Corinthians 2:2–4 shows Paul was manipulative in causing sorrow to control the church. What does 2 Corinthians 2:2–4 actually teach?
options: Paul's sorrowful communication was motivated by genuine love and pastoral concern, not manipulation
Paul intentionally caused grief to dominate the church
Paul's letters were purely rhetorical with no emotional involvement
Paul avoided all confrontation to keep peace at any cost
questions.correctAnswer: Paul's sorrowful communication was motivated by genuine love and pastoral concern, not manipulation
questions.explanation: Verses 2–4 show Paul sorrowed because he loved them and feared causing grief, revealing pastoral heart rather than manipulative intent.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Corinthians 2:3 teach about apostolic confidence in the church's spiritual state?
options: Apostolic confidence is based on the joy and obedience evident in the believers
Apostolic confidence is unconditional and ignores the church's failings
Apostolic confidence is irrelevant to ministry effectiveness
Apostolic confidence depends solely on external success
questions.correctAnswer: Apostolic confidence is based on the joy and obedience evident in the believers
questions.explanation: Verse 3 shows Paul wrote to avoid sorrow from those he should rejoice in, indicating his confidence is grounded in the church's spiritual health.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 2 Corinthians 2:17 demonstrate through Paul's ministry?
questions.correctAnswer: Sincerity
questions.explanation: Verse 17 contrasts Paul's ministry with corruptors, emphasizing sincerity in speaking before God through Christ, highlighting God's attribute of sincerity expressed through His servants.

questions.question: How does 2 Corinthians 2:12–13 relate to the theme of divine guidance and human restlessness in ministry narratives throughout Scripture?
options: It illustrates the tension between open doors of opportunity and inner spiritual unrest when plans are delayed
It teaches that ministry is always peaceful and without difficulty
It denies any role of human emotions in ministry
It suggests divine guidance is irrelevant to apostolic missions
questions.correctAnswer: It illustrates the tension between open doors of opportunity and inner spiritual unrest when plans are delayed
questions.explanation: Paul's experience in verses 12–13 shows a door opened but no rest due to Titus's absence, reflecting biblical themes of faithful obedience amid uncertainty (cf. Acts 16).

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 2 Corinthians 2:8 and 2 Corinthians 2:9 teach about love and obedience in the Christian community?
options: Confirmed love toward the repentant one tests the community's obedience in all things
Love and obedience are unrelated in church discipline
Obedience is required but love is optional
Love can replace the need for obedience
questions.correctAnswer: Confirmed love toward the repentant one tests the community's obedience in all things
questions.explanation: Verse 8 urges confirming love, and verse 9 states the letter was written to test obedience, teaching love and obedience are integrally connected in the church.
